Hi Sean,

Thanks for the initial packet. A couple of follow-ups from our identity and procurement teams — we've pasted the questions below for clarity. Can you confirm whether: 1) Redwood supports SCIM bulk provisioning for group membership and custom attributes (entitlements) with delta and full syncs; 2) SCIM rate limits and throttling behavior for enterprise customers (we run ~150k provisioning events/day); 3) SSO flows: do you support both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated SAML and OIDC native flows; 4) Admin model: can we delegate tenant-scoped admin roles without granting global org permissions, and do you retain admin audit trails for at least 365 days?

Also attaching our RFI template. We prefer a short call to walk through the answers next week.

NovusBank

From: sean_gallagher@redwoodai.com
To: Sarah Lane <sarah.lane@novusbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodai.com, ben_carter@redwoodai.com, kimberly_park@redwoodai.com
Date: 2026-09-12T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Identity attribute mapping + admin controls follow-up

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Answers below and I attached a completed RFI and an attribute matrix for NovusBank's review (scim_attribute_matrix.csv). Quick summary:

- SCIM provisioning: Redwood supports SCIM 2.0 with both delta (PATCH) and full (PUT) syncs. We include group membership and custom attribute mapping (entitlements) via configurable attribute maps. We also support bulk provisioning endpoints for initial seed jobs.
- Throttling / rate limits: Enterprise Dedicated customers can request raised SCIM throughput. Default hosted tier enforces 120 req/min, but Dedicated / Private deployments are configurable; we offer burst allowances and token-bucket policing. For 150k events/day we typically recommend a Dedicated pool and a short lived queue for initial bulk imports.
- SSO flows: We support SP-initiated and IdP-initiated SAML v2.0 and OIDC (authorization code + PKCE). Both SP- and IdP-initiated flows are supported for web & mobile.
- Admin model & RBAC: Tenant-scoped roles are supported. Our RBAC separates global organization admins from tenant-level delegates (Admin, ReadOnlyAdmin, BillingAdmin). Delegated admins can be scoped to one or more tenants without global privileges.
- Audit retention: Audit logs for admin actions and auth events retained by default for 365 days in Dedicated; hosted customers can purchase extended retention or route logs to your SIEM. Logs include who changed role mappings, SCIM provisioning deltas, and SAML metadata exchanges.

I'll note a few items where Marissa (Product) may provide technical detail. Proposed next step: 30-minute call to walk the SCIM matrix and tenant-role mapping Tuesday 13th at 10:00am ET. If that works, we'll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachments: novus_rfi_template_filled.pdf, scim_attribute_matrix.csv

Forwarding Sarah's email — quick clarifications for the scim throttle wording we send:

Marissa here — product notes:
- For Dedicated, SCIM endpoint capacity is configurable per pool; we support token-based parallelization and provide a SCIM job API that accepts CSV payloads and runs async if you need steady-state > 20k/day.
- For bulk initial imports we recommend our async bulk endpoint (max payloads ~10k users per job) and supply an ingest status API.
- Delta semantics: we preserve your canonical source-of-truth mapping; our PATCH semantics support group operations (add/remove) and we record per-change metadata (who, when, source).

Kimberly — can you add a short blurb on how audit logs are stored and the encryption-at-rest key handling (KMS) for Dedicated?

-M

From: kimberly_park@redwoodai.com

Subject: Re: Fwd: RFI: attribute mapping + admin controls — scim throttling details

Thanks — internal note on logs and keys for external answer:

- Audit logs: Stored in an append-only ledger in our telemetry store; entries include event_type, actor_id, target_resource, and change_set (SCIM patch details when applicable).
- Retention: 365 days default for Dedicated; configurable up to 7 years for Enterprise Private deployments.
- Encryption & keys: Logs are encrypted at rest using AES-256; keys managed by customer KMS (bring-your-own-key) in Private/Dedicated, or Redwood-managed KMS with HSM-backed keys in Hosted.
- Tamper evidence: We provide signed digests of daily log batches for compliance scans.

I'll draft a short paragraph for Sarah that includes the KMS/BYOK options.

-Kimberly

Tom/Sarah — quick answers:

1) Metadata automation:
- SAML: Redwood supports optional metadata auto-fetch from a reachable metadata URL and verifies certificate chains. We also support manual upload of IdP metadata where required by compliance.
- OIDC: We support JWKS auto-rotation and will fetch well-known configuration endpoints. JWKS keys are cached and rotated; rotation events are logged in the audit trail.

2) Admin scoping:
- Yes — delegated roles can be scoped to resource subsets (user lifecycle, groups, provisioning only). We model roles as (namespace, role, resource-scopes). Billing operations are a distinct capability; tenant admins do not receive billing privileges unless explicitly granted BillingAdmin.

Attached is a simple RBAC diagram (admin-roles-mapping.xlsx) and the SCIM matrix for your review. Proposed slots: Sept 16 at 10:00am ET or Sept 17 at 09:30am ET. I can send an invite for the 16th 10:00am ET if that works.
